audit_items.proof_trace: The `record_attendance_by_card` SQL function uses a non-atomic READ COMMITTED SELECT-then-INSERT pattern (L42-50) with no time-window guard, no advisory lock, and no SERIALIZABLE isolation. Two concurrent calls for the same card_id can both read the same `v_last_type` before either commits, then both insert the same attendance type — creating a duplicate record and corrupting the toggle state. The client-side `processing` guard (kiosk/page.tsx:343-345) blocks sequential UI-driven double-submission but is trivially bypassed since the RPC is directly accessible to the `anon` role (`GRANT EXECUTE` in 20260317000001_fix_security_permissions.sql:102).
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker (or malicious script) calls `supabase.schema('attendance').rpc('record_attendance_by_card', { p_card_id: '<target_card>' })` twice concurrently from any unauthenticated client; both calls select the same last type before either commits and both insert identical attendance records, corrupting the user's check-in/check-out state.
